clue.text: Opportunity to cut north, say, for point on top

indicators.note: to cut means the letter for north is cut out of the opportunity word

parts.note: a window is an opportunity, a window of time to act
N is the compass abbreviation for north
to speak is to say

explanation.surface: Someone sees a chance to trim off the northern part, perhaps to make a point at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N out of WINDOW to leave WIDOW, then add SPEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow's peak is the V-shaped point formed by a hairline dipping down at the centre of the forehead, a point on top of the head.

clue.text: Area with vice amongst company?

indicators.note: amongst places area and vice between the two letters for company

parts.note: a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A question about a place where wickedness sits among a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: A and SIN go between C and O; read whole, the clue also describes the place: a gambling area where vice is found among company.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling establishment, a place where the vice of betting happens in a crowd.

clue.text: Older relative eats last of pitta bread

indicators.note: eats means the relative takes the next letter inside her

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of pitta

parts.note: pitta supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Grandma polishes off the end of the pitta bread.
explanation.walkthrough: A, the last letter of pitta, goes inside NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, baked in a tandoor oven.

clue.text: This might be deadly Russian or French character, finally getting comeuppance?

indicators.note: in a down answer the final letter comes up, moving from the bottom to the top of the column

parts.note: ou is the French word for or
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A French character finally gets what's coming to them, perhaps in a deadly Russian game.
explanation.walkthrough: OU and LETTER make OULETTER; its final R comes up to the top of this down entry. 'Russian' does double duty with the definition rather than giving a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is the potentially lethal game of firing a revolver loaded with one round at one's own head.

clue.text: End of school period

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a limit or finishing point, as in a lease coming to ...
second meaning: a division of the school year

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the last day of school, but 'End' and 'school period' are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a set limit or conclusion and one of the divisions of an academic year.

clue.text: Graduates tracking the greatest caveman?

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the graduates come after the boxer

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
BA (Bachelor of Arts) twice gives graduates

explanation.surface: Graduates following the greatest caveman, perhaps an evolutionary study.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, billed himself 'The Greatest'. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba discovers the forty thieves' treasure cave with 'Open Sesame', making him a cave man.

clue.text: Actor's actor, someone chivalrous?

parts.note: a person, any one, gives A
a gent, a gentleman, is someone chivalrous

explanation.surface: A question about an actor's actor, someone gallant.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A GENT for the wordplay. The definition plays on two senses: a performer's representative, and one who acts.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical agent represents performers, and an agent is also, literally, one who acts on another's behalf.

clue.text: E.g. Norma Jeane, ultimately a pro after surgery

indicators.note: after surgery the letters have been operated on and rearranged
ultimately picks the last letter of Jeane

parts.note: Jeane supplies its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe, born Norma Jeane, as a professional after cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norma Jeane' looks like one name, Marilyn Monroe's, but the definition stops at 'Norma', the Bellini opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's tragic opera about a Druid priestess, so it is an example of the musical-drama genre.

clue.text: A number wearing symbol of Aviator shades

indicators.note: wearing means the number has the pilot's emblem around it

parts.note: pilots wear wings as their badge

explanation.surface: A number wearing the badge of a pilot's sunglasses, the Ray-Ban Aviator style.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then N inside WINGS. Aviator sunglasses make 'shades' look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Awnings are canopies over windows or shopfronts that provide shade from the sun.

clue.text: Sit-in possibly cracked dome

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Protesters, maybe in a sit-in, have cracked a dome.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a protest demonstration, and a sit-in is one kind of protest.

clue.text: I mingle restlessly with fan fiction writer

indicators.note: restlessly means the letters keep moving about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mingles uneasily with a writer of fan fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan fiction writer' reads as one phrase, but 'fan' is fodder and 'fiction writer' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming was the novelist who created James Bond.

clue.text: What shows canal barges etc — oops! Duck gets caught

indicators.note: gets caught means the zero is trapped within the rearranged letters
barges means jostles roughly, knocking the letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Canal boats collide, someone cries oops, and a duck is trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal barges' reads as a phrase, but the canal is the ear canal, and 'barges' is a verb meaning jostles.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is a medical instrument for looking into the ear canal.

clue.text: Failure of Eastern educational standards to take over

indicators.note: to take means the three Rs take another letter inside them

parts.note: the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A failure of Eastern schooling standards to win through.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the basics of schooling: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a failure to get something right.

clue.text: Label that's carrying name for dish

parts.note: a tag is a label

indicators.note: carrying means the letters for that's hold the name abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A label carrying the name of a dish, as on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after its conical earthenware pot.

clue.text: SEAL waging wars from northern city

indicators.note: wars here is the verb, battles, setting the letters fighting into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Navy SEALs waging wars from a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waging wars' looks like a set phrase, but 'waging' is fodder and 'wars' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaswegian describes a native of Glasgow, Scotland's largest city, in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Disc engine's case used for thruster?

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: case means the outside of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: engine gives its outer letters

explanation.surface: A technical query about a disc engine's housing in a spacecraft thruster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description: the sword is not a rocket thruster but something that thrusts.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a fencing sword used for thrusting, scoring only with the point.

clue.text: Cane found in sort of purple fruit

indicators.note: found in means the cane goes inside the purple word

parts.note: puce is a brownish-purple colour
a rod is a cane, a stick

explanation.surface: A sugar cane discovered inside a purple fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce is farm output, especially fruit and vegetables, and fruit can stand for the yield of labour.

clue.text: Eager to play match

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters frolic about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone keen to take part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture, but it is a verb meaning tally.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to correspond or tally, as when two accounts match.

clue.text: Creativity shown by Dire Straits, short of opening tracks

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, so the letters are in a terrible mess
short of opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Straits loses its first letter
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: The band Dire Straits show creativity, though they lack an opening track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of opening' leaves TRAITS, which 'Dire' rearranges; the band name hides both the anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or talent in an art.

clue.text: Prodigal son's covering this as well

indicators.note: covering means the outer words wrap around the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: The prodigal son's coat covers this too.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is an adverb meaning in addition, too.

clue.text: Surprise! Alien leaves

parts.note: to rock is to shock or surprise
ET is the alien in the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An exclamation as an alien departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the verb of departing; it is the salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket, also called arugula, is a peppery salad plant eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: Sitcom star

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British science-fiction sitcom set aboard a spaceship
second meaning: a small, cool, faint star

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the star of a sitcom, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Dwarf is a long-running BBC comedy in space, and in astronomy a red dwarf is a small low-mass star.

clue.text: Long-distance runner called an Uber for a stretch

indicators.note: for a stretch says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A marathon runner ordered a taxi for part of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but a river runs too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube flows nearly 3,000 km across Europe, a long-distance river.

clue.text: Bug biting foot and arm

indicators.note: biting means the annoying word grips the foot abbreviation in its jaws

parts.note: to bug is to annoy, rile

explanation.surface: An insect bites someone's foot and arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect; it is the verb, to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a firearm, and arm means a weapon.

clue.text: Refuse to go into this new B&B, in hubris

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, gives the two Bs
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A proud owner refuses to go into a newly opened bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish bin is the container that refuse, or waste, is put into.

clue.text: Sacred text omitting black humour

indicators.note: omitting means one letter is left out of the holy book

parts.note: the Bible is the Christian sacred text
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A holy book without any dark comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black humour' reads as one phrase, but 'black' gives B and 'humour' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bile was one of the four bodily humours of old medicine, linked with an angry temper.

clue.text: Recovered missing non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: missing means the abstainer's letters are absent

parts.note: someone who has recovered from illness is better
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A recovering patient goes without a non-alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-alcoholic drink' reads as one phrase, but 'non-alcoholic' gives TT and the bare 'drink' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic beverage brewed from malted grain and hops.

clue.text: Shortly slip home

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a gaffe is a slip, a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone will soon slip off home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon'; it means the next word is cut short. Gaff is British slang for one's home or house.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a gaff is a house or flat, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Swiss genius who uses Grease in audition

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the oiler's sound gives the spelling

parts.note: an oiler is someone who greases machinery

explanation.surface: A Swiss genius auditions for a part in the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is said 'oiler'. 'Grease' suggests the musical, but it is lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician of enormous influence.

clue.text: Hold me back, British people

indicators.note: back means the word me is turned round

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: A plea to restrain me, addressed to the British public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold me back' sounds like a request for restraint; 'Hold' is the definition and 'me back' gives EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to clasp or hug them in one's arms.
